subject.title: Bug: Telegram delivery queue recovery can replay old sendMessage replies and duplicate delivery-mirror transcript entries

question: For legacy pending Telegram delivery-queue rows that lack `recoveryState` but have ambiguous send failure evidence, should recovery prioritize avoiding duplicate sends or preserving possible undelivered messages?
rationale: Both outcomes have user-visible cost, and current main plus the open ambiguous-delivery PR show this is a maintainer policy decision rather than a purely mechanical cleanup.

options.title: Map legacy rows to unknown-send policy
options.body: Backfill or classify ambiguous legacy Telegram rows so they cannot be blindly replayed and can follow the same reconciliation/quarantine behavior as newly marked rows.

options.title: Quarantine ambiguous legacy rows
options.body: Move old Telegram rows with network/timeout send errors and no recovery state to failed diagnostics to minimize duplicate delivery risk.

options.title: Keep legacy rows replayable
options.body: Accept duplicate-send risk for old rows to maximize recovery of messages that may not have reached Telegram.

recommendation.title: Map legacy rows to unknown-send policy
recommendation.body: Backfill or classify ambiguous legacy Telegram rows so they cannot be blindly replayed and can follow the same reconciliation/quarantine behavior as newly marked rows.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter is the strongest current-history owner for the exact recovery, migration, and Telegram mirror code ranges that need the policy encoded.
